i) tapping India's diverse geographic potential
ii) deeper rural market penetration
iii) rising engagement with new-to-credit (NTC) customers
iv) accelerated digital adoption.

These levers coupled with huge unmet demand are expected to propel gross loan portfolio (GLP) to grow at 15%+ CAGR, reaching INR 10 trillion over the next 5-6 years.

We believe the industry will return to its historical cross-cyclical ROEs of 20% over the next 5-6 years

Money Control on SJS Enterprises: Strong Q4 FY25, new products, clients growth drivers

One of the company’s key growth drivers is the rising demand for premium vehicles, including big cars, SUVs, and high-end bikes, now extending to the consumer durable segment.

As per the management, the content per vehicle is expected to rise 4-6x from the current level of Rs 3,500-5,000 per vehicle.

New clients offer significant opportunities

In Q1FY25, SJS on-boarded Dixon Technologies as a client. It operates in the consumer electronics, lighting, home appliances, and mobile phone segments.

SJS has already started small-scale supplies to Dixon, and the management has indicated a significant opportunity that could be a key growth lever for the next phase of growth.

In April 2025, the company on-boarded Hero Motocorp as its client to supply decal and logos for many models. The management indicated that HMCL sources these products worth Rs 250 crore annually, a significant part of which should flow to SJS.

Julius Bar on Union Budget 2025-2026 - Consumption Booster; Good summary of Sector related impact

The Budget, at a margin, has been a non-event from capital markets perspective

The economic activity levels slowed during 2024 due to elections disruptive rainfall. With these drags in the base and government spending supporting consumption, the earnings growth is set to improve to 12-13% in FY26E

Sectors with double-digit earnings growth include industrials, property, banks, two-wheelers, and telecoms.

Overall, we continue to remain constructive on the Indian equity markets, driven by earnings cycle and strong domestic liquidity, coupled with likely comeback of FPI flows. Markets could be volatile in H1CY25, as debates persist around Donald Trump policies and comeback of India’s earnings growth momentum. We would recommend to buy the potential ‘dips’.

MSCI November Rejig: Nuvama Sees Boost In HDFC Bank Weightage, Inclusion Of Adani Energy

The November round of rejig in MSCI indices may lead to a boost in HDFC Bank Ltd.'s weightage, according to Nuvama Alternative & Quantitative Research.

HDFC Bank could attract inflows amounting to $1.88 billion, Nuvama said in a report released on Tuesday, two days before the scheduled rejig of the MSCI indices. The private lender is included under the MSCI Global Standard Index.

As per Nuvama's forecast, Adani Energy Solutions Ltd., along with Kalyan Jewellers Ltd., Oberoi Realty Ltd., and Alkem Laboratories Ltd., could be added to the index. Among the probable additions is also BSE Ltd., one of the two main stock exchanges in India.

The official announcement on the adjustments in the MSCI indices is scheduled at 2:30 a.m. (IST) on Nov. 7. The rejig will come into effect on Nov. 25.
